content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text assigns UNDERDETERMINED to the Matthew 1:20 point, so it is a ruling governed by K-S2's bar on using single-verse nonstatement or two-sense openness as a ground for UNDERDETERMINED.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D2 vs C1 (Matthew 1:20): UNDERDETERMINED -- the challenger's covenant-origin analogy is footed (1 Chronicles 28:6, Acts 1:8) but the sentence's own words state the source of what is in the womb; answered in [CR3] LINK 2.","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.","room":"I weighed whether \"A verse that carries two senses at once is not open\" makes the judge's mention of a footed covenant-origin analogy plus the verse's own stated source a two-sense verse where both stand, or whether UNDERDETERMINED merely rests on the single verse's silence about covenant-origin.","why":"The judge calls the point UNDERDETERMINED while treating Matthew 1:20 as carrying both a footed covenant-origin analogy and its own stated source, so it leaves open what K-S2 says is not open and both senses stand."}
